text:
zoe: Heads-up 10am canary summary: we ran asymmetric-batcher + kernel-spin-throttle across a mixed prod-like pool. Short-chat p99 dropped ~15% (210ms -> 178ms) and cost per 1M tokens looks down ~12% on initial estimates. Bandwidth-bound workloads also show fewer kernel launches. :tada:

pranav: Huge, nice work. Any negative tradeoffs?

rachel (perf): No correctness/regression on the eval sets (chat-200 / assistant-open). We did observe a small throughput dip for long-context streaming (>12k tokens) on machines without NVLink aggregation. Looks like our throttle is too aggressive when the kernel queue is already saturated. Filed PERF-499 and attached traces.

matt (infra): Hmm ok. Which knob controls that? I can flip it for the affected fleet if needed.

zoe: It's `kernel_spin_throttle_ms`. Canary used 4ms. We also enabled asymmetric batching so short requests are favored into microbatches and long ones into isolated lanes. That combination reduced wakeups and improved tail.

ci-bot: perf summary (baseline -> canary):
- short-chat (avg seq 96): p50 30ms -> 26ms, p95 95ms -> 82ms, p99 210ms -> 178ms
- conv-long (avg seq 1024): p50 150ms -> 142ms, p95 430ms -> 420ms, p99 980ms -> 1010ms (regression on p99 for long-context)
- throughput: overall +4% but long-context throughput -6% on non-NVLink boxes
All CI checks: pass

pranav: Can we adjust the throttle dynamically based on detected NVLink capability? If so we could keep gains for NVLink fleets and relax for others.

rachel (perf): Good call. I'll add a capability check and make the default fallback 1ms on non-NVLink nodes. Also adding an auto-rollback alert: if short-chat p99 > 230ms then trigger.

zoe: Sample canary config we used (for release notes):
```yaml
feature: asymmetric-batcher-v2
canary_percent: 12
knobs:
  asymmetric_threshold_len: 256
  kernel_spin_throttle_ms: 4
  microbatch_max_size: 8
fallback: stable-release-2026-03
```

matt (infra): I'll add a staged flag so ops can flip `kernel_spin_throttle_ms` per pool. Also creating a short runbook: fallback route -> stable-release-2026-03, rollback flag -> ff_asymm_batcher_v2=false.

pranav: Please put a blurb in #release-notes and a short post in #all-hands noting the ~12% cost improvement estimate and the PERF-499 caveat.

rachel (perf): Tests to run before full rollout: web-chat-200, background-batch-peak, long-context-smoke. I'll schedule canary2 with dynamic-throttle tomorrow AM.

deploy-bot: Canary started (12% traffic). Initial healthchecks: ok.

zoe: Thanks team. If canary2 removes the long-context p99 bump we'll proceed with a 100% rollout by EOD. Otherwise we flip throttle per pool and document the nuance. :thumbsup:
